products.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
products.source:
* Organization administrators can authenticate external OAuth applications to UiPath using JWTs from third-party identity providers like GitHub Actions or Azure Managed Identity, without needing a client secret.
* Added a data region confirmation workflow that allows administrators to review and confirm their organization and tenant data regions.
* Introduced automatic deletion of inactive community organizations after 90 days of inactivity, with advance notifications and a recovery window.
* You can change the tenant region directly from the Admin portal without raising a support ticket with UiPath.
* UiPath has paused the transition of Automation Cloud Portal outbound IP ranges for Customer-Managed Keys until at least June 2026 - ensure both existing and upcoming IP ranges are allowed in your firewall.
* You can now bring your own LLM configuration for Autopilot through the AI Trust Layer.

analysis.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
analysis.summary: Administration capabilities were expanded across authentication, data region management, tenant region changes, and organization lifecycle controls. The notes also announce a pause in the outbound IP range transition for Customer-Managed Keys and advise customers to allow both current and upcoming IP ranges.
analysis.overall_analysis: These changes strengthen administrative control, reduce support dependency for region management, and improve security and governance options for cloud organizations. The IP range pause is operationally significant for customers using Customer-Managed Keys because firewall configurations must accommodate both existing and future ranges during the extended transition period.

changes.name: JWT-based authentication for external OAuth applications
changes.summary: Organization administrators can authenticate external OAuth applications to UiPath using JWTs from third-party identity providers such as GitHub Actions or Azure Managed Identity, without requiring a client secret.
changes.analysis: This likely improves security and simplifies machine-to-machine authentication by enabling secretless or reduced-secret integration patterns with external identity providers.
changes.impact: Organization administrators and teams integrating external OAuth applications with UiPath, especially those using GitHub Actions or Azure Managed Identity.

changes.name: Data region confirmation workflow
changes.summary: A data region confirmation workflow was added so administrators can review and confirm their organization and tenant data regions.
changes.analysis: This likely supports governance, compliance, and clearer administrative oversight of where data is stored.
changes.impact: Administrators responsible for compliance, governance, and tenant configuration.

changes.name: Automatic deletion of inactive community organizations
changes.summary: Inactive community organizations are automatically deleted after 90 days of inactivity, with advance notifications and a recovery window.
changes.analysis: This likely helps manage unused community environments and reduce dormant organization sprawl while giving users notice and a chance to recover.
changes.impact: Community organization administrators and users of inactive community organizations.

changes.name: Tenant region changes from the Admin portal
changes.summary: Administrators can now change the tenant region directly from the Admin portal without opening a support ticket with UiPath.
changes.analysis: This reduces operational friction and gives administrators more direct control over tenant configuration.
changes.impact: Tenant and organization administrators managing regional setup.

changes.name: Pause of Automation Cloud Portal outbound IP range transition for Customer-Managed Keys
changes.summary: UiPath has paused the transition of Automation Cloud Portal outbound IP ranges for Customer-Managed Keys until at least June 2026, and customers must allow both existing and upcoming IP ranges in their firewall.
changes.analysis: This is an important operational update for network and security planning, helping avoid connectivity or access issues during the delayed transition period.
changes.impact: Customers using Customer-Managed Keys, especially security and infrastructure teams managing firewall rules.
